newsitem.title: UK: Labour declines comments on BOE reports.
newsitem.headline: Labour declines comments on BOE reports.

text.p: A spokesman for Gordon Brown, who is expected to be Chancellor of the Exchequer in Britain's new Labour government, declined to comment on reports that new appointments would be made at the top of the Bank of England.
A news organisation reported that Howard Davies, current deputy governor, would become Governor in place of Eddie George and that Gavyn Davies, chief economist at Goldman Sachs, would be his deputy.
Brown's spokesman laughed when asked about the reports and said that since Brown had not yet been made Chancellor, there could be no question of him making appointments at the Bank.
A Bank spokeswoman noted that Eddie George holds a five-year contract which does not expire until June 30, 1998 while Howard Davies's appointment runs until September 10, 2000.
She refused to comment on the news story.
